lessons.title: Skewers and Satay: Meat and Vegetable Options
lessons.body: Skewers are one of the easiest and most profitable street foods. You need bamboo skewers (soak in water 30 minutes to prevent burning), a grill or charcoal stove, and a good marinade. For meat, use beef, chicken, or goat cut into 2-3 cm cubes. A simple African marinade: 1 cup oil, 1/2 cup soy sauce, 1/4 cup vinegar, 4 cloves garlic (minced), 1 tbsp ginger (grated), 1 tsp chili flakes, salt and pepper. Marinate meat for at least 2 hours, preferably overnight in a fridge. For vegetables, use onions, bell peppers, tomatoes, mushrooms, and zucchini cut into chunks. Thread meat and vegetables alternately onto skewers, leaving a small gap between pieces so they cook evenly. Grill over medium-high heat (charcoal should be grey with ash) for 8-12 minutes, turning every 2 minutes. For chicken, ensure internal temperature reaches 75Â°C. For satay, make a peanut sauce: 1 cup roasted peanuts (ground), 1 cup coconut milk, 2 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tbsp palm sugar, 1 tsp chili paste, 1 tbsp lime juice. Simmer all for 5 minutes. Serve skewers with the sauce. In Africa, you can use local spices like suya mix (ground peanuts, ginger, paprika, cayenne) for a Nigerian-style skewer. For vegetables, brush with oil and grill 5-7 minutes until charred. Sell skewers in sets of 3-5 on a paper plate with a side of sauce. Cost per skewer: about 50-70% profit margin if you buy meat in bulk. Keep raw and cooked separate to avoid contamination. Always wash hands and tools after handling raw meat.

lessons.title: Fried Chicken: Korean, Southern, and Japanese Styles
lessons.body: Fried chicken is a global favourite. You need a deep pot, oil (vegetable or groundnut), a thermometer, and a wire rack. For all styles, start with chicken pieces (drumsticks, wings, thighs) seasoned with salt and pepper. For Southern style: make a buttermilk brine (2 cups buttermilk + 1 tbsp hot sauce) and soak chicken 4 hours. Dredge in flour mixed with 1 tbsp paprika, 1 tsp garlic powder, 1 tsp onion powder, 1 tsp cayenne, salt and pepper. Fry at 165Â°C for 12-15 minutes until golden and internal temp 75Â°C. For Korean style: use a thin batter of 1 cup flour, 1 cup cornstarch, 1 tsp baking powder, 1 cup cold water, 2 tbsp soy sauce. Fry once at 160Â°C for 8 minutes, then double-fry at 190Â°C for 3 minutes for extra crunch. Toss in a sauce: 2 tbsp gochujang, 2 tbsp honey, 1 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tbsp rice vinegar, 1 tbsp sesame oil, minced garlic. For Japanese karaage: marinate chicken in 2 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tbsp sake (or dry white wine), 1 tbsp ginger juice, 1 tsp sugar for 30 minutes. Coat in potato starch or cornstarch. Fry at 170Â°C for 4-5 minutes until light golden. In Africa, you can use cassava flour for a gluten-free crunch. Always fry in batches to keep oil temperature stable. Drain on a wire rack, not paper, to keep crispy. Serve with lemon wedges, chili sauce, or mayo. Cost: use local chicken, buy whole and cut yourself to save money. Oil can be reused 3-4 times if strained and stored cool.

lessons.title: French Fries and Loaded Fries
lessons.body: French fries are a top seller. Use starchy potatoes like Russet or local Irish potatoes. Wash, peel, and cut into 1 cm thick sticks. Soak in cold water for 30 minutes to remove excess starch. Dry completely with a clean cloth. Heat oil to 150Â°C (low-medium). Fry potatoes for 5-6 minutes until soft but not brown. Remove and let cool for 10 minutes. Then heat oil to 190Â°C (high). Fry again for 2-3 minutes until golden and crispy. This double-fry method gives the best texture. Salt immediately after frying. For loaded fries: top hot fries with melted cheese (cheddar or local cheese), cooked minced meat, chopped onions, jalapeÃ±os, and a drizzle of mayo and ketchup. For a African twist, use suya spice, grilled chicken bits, and a spicy pepper sauce. You can also make masala fries: sprinkle with curry powder, chili powder, and salt. To keep fries hot for sale, hold under a heat lamp or in a warmer, but never cover tightly or they steam and get soggy. For large batches, pre-fry the first stage, cool, and store in fridge for up to 24 hours. Then fry to order. Oil temperature is critical: too low and fries absorb oil; too high and they burn outside while raw inside. Use a thermometer. Change oil when it darkens or smokes. Serve in paper cones or boxes with a fork. Profit margin is high: a 50 kg bag of potatoes makes many servings. Buy potatoes in bulk from local markets. Add seasoning like rosemary salt or peri-peri for variety.

lessons.title: Onion Rings and Tempura
lessons.body: Onion rings and tempura are crispy, light, and cheap to make. For onion rings: slice large onions into 1 cm rings, separate. For the batter: 1 cup flour, 1 tsp baking powder, 1 tsp salt, 1 tsp paprika, 1 cup cold water or beer. Mix until just combined (lumps are fine). Dip rings in batter, then fry at 180Â°C for 2-3 minutes until golden. Drain on a rack. For extra crunch, coat in breadcrumbs after batter. For tempura: use a light batter of 1 cup flour, 1 cup ice-cold water, 1 egg yolk. Mix lightly; do not overmix. Dip vegetables (sweet potato slices, green beans, cauliflower, pumpkin) or shrimp. Fry at 175Â°C for 2-3 minutes until light and crispy. Tempura should be pale, not brown. Serve with tentsuyu sauce: 1/4 cup soy sauce, 1/4 cup mirin (or honey), 1/4 cup dashi (or water), grated ginger. In Africa, you can use local vegetables like plantain, okra, and yam. For onion rings, a spicy mayo dip: 1/2 cup mayo, 2 tbsp ketchup, 1 tsp chili sauce, 1 tsp paprika. Keep oil clean: strain after each use. For volume sales, pre-batter onion rings and freeze on a tray, then fry from frozen at 180Â°C for 3-4 minutes. Tempura batter must be used immediately; discard after 30 minutes. Serve in paper bags with a dip. Cost per serving is low, making these high-profit items. Experiment with local flours like cassava or maize for gluten-free versions.

lessons.title: Grilled Corn and Elote
lessons.body: Grilled corn is a simple, high-margin street food. Use fresh sweet corn or maize. Remove husks and silk, then grill over medium-high charcoal (grey ash) for 10-12 minutes, turning every 2 minutes until kernels are charred in spots. Brush with butter or oil during grilling. For elote (Mexican street corn): grill corn, then slather with a mixture of 1/2 cup mayo, 1/2 cup sour cream (or yoghurt), 1 cup crumbled cotija cheese (or feta), 1 tsp chili powder, 1 tsp garlic powder, juice of 1 lime, salt. Roll corn in the mixture, then sprinkle with more cheese and chili powder. Serve with a lime wedge. For a African twist, use a spicy peanut sauce: 1/2 cup ground roasted peanuts, 1 tbsp chili paste, 1 tbsp honey, 1 tbsp soy sauce, 2 tbsp water. Or a peri-peri butter: 1/2 cup butter, 2 tbsp peri-peri sauce, 1 tsp garlic. Grill corn, brush with peri-peri butter. You can also boil corn first for 5 minutes to speed up grilling. For large events, pre-grill corn and hold in a warmer. Sell corn on the cob or cut kernels into cups. For cups: cut kernels off grilled corn, top with butter, cheese, chili, and lime. Cost per cob is low; selling price can be 3-4 times cost. Use a sharp knife to cut kernels. Always wear gloves when handling hot corn. Provide toothpicks or forks. Keep corn warm in a cooler with a hot water bottle or in a chafing dish. Experiment with different seasonings: curry powder, smoked paprika, or suya spice.

lessons.title: Dipping Sauces and Seasonings
lessons.body: Great dipping sauces turn simple fried and grilled foods into memorable meals. You need a few base recipes and then vary them. For a universal spicy mayo: 1 cup mayonnaise, 2 tbsp ketchup, 1 tbsp hot sauce (like Tabasco), 1 tsp paprika, 1 tsp garlic powder, 1 tsp lime juice. Mix well. For a garlic aioli: 1 cup mayo, 4 cloves garlic (minced), 1 tbsp lemon juice, salt and pepper. For a sweet chili sauce: 1/2 cup sugar, 1/2 cup water, 1/4 cup rice vinegar, 2 tbsp chili flakes, 2 cloves garlic (minced), 1 tbsp cornstarch mixed with 2 tbsp water. Simmer sugar, water, vinegar, chili, and garlic for 5 minutes, then add cornstarch slurry and cook until thickened. For a peanut sauce: 1 cup peanut butter, 1/2 cup coconut milk, 2 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tbsp honey, 1 tbsp lime juice, 1 tsp chili paste. Whisk over low heat until smooth. For a yoghurt mint sauce: 1 cup yoghurt, 2 tbsp chopped mint, 1 tbsp lemon juice, 1 clove garlic (minced), salt. For dry seasonings: suya spice (ground peanuts, ginger, paprika, cayenne, salt), peri-peri (chili, garlic, lemon, oil), or a simple salt and pepper mix with paprika and garlic powder. Store sauces in squeeze bottles or small containers. Label and date. Keep cold sauces refrigerated; discard after 3 days. For fried foods, offer at least two dips: one creamy, one spicy. For grilled meats, offer a chimichurri: 1 cup parsley, 1/2 cup oil, 1/4 cup vinegar, 4 cloves garlic, 1 tsp chili flakes, salt. In Africa, use local ingredients like tamarind, groundnut, and scotch bonnet. Test your sauces with a small group before selling. Portion control: 30-50 ml per serving. Charge extra for premium dips. Always maintain hygiene: use clean spoons, never double-dip.

quiz.q: What is the main purpose of soaking bamboo skewers in water before grilling?
options: A) To make them easier to thread
B) To prevent them from burning
quiz.explanation: Soaking skewers in water prevents them from catching fire on the grill.

quiz.q: What internal temperature should chicken reach to be safe to eat?
quiz.explanation: Chicken must be cooked to 75Â°C to ensure harmful bacteria are killed.

quiz.q: Which ingredient is NOT typically in a peanut sauce for satay?
quiz.explanation: Tomato paste is not a traditional ingredient in satay peanut sauce.

quiz.q: For Southern fried chicken, what is the recommended oil temperature for frying?
quiz.explanation: 165Â°C is ideal for even cooking and a crispy crust without burning.

quiz.q: What makes Korean fried chicken extra crunchy?
quiz.explanation: Double-frying at different temperatures creates a very crispy texture.

quiz.q: Which starch is traditionally used for Japanese karaage coating?
quiz.explanation: Potato starch gives karaage its light, crispy coating.

quiz.q: What is the first step in making French fries to ensure crispiness?
quiz.explanation: Soaking removes excess starch, which helps fries become crispy.

quiz.q: At what temperature should you do the second fry for French fries?
quiz.explanation: A high temperature of 190Â°C gives fries a golden, crispy exterior.

quiz.q: What is a common topping for loaded fries?
quiz.explanation: Melted cheese is a classic topping for loaded fries.

quiz.q: For onion rings, what type of batter is recommended?
quiz.explanation: A thin batter creates a light, crispy coating for onion rings.

quiz.q: What is the key to making tempura batter crispy?
quiz.explanation: Ice-cold water prevents gluten development, resulting in a light, crispy tempura.

quiz.q: Which vegetable is NOT typically used in tempura?
quiz.explanation: Tomato is too watery and does not hold up well in tempura batter.

quiz.q: What is elote?
options: A) Grilled corn with spicy mayo and cheese
quiz.explanation: Elote is Mexican street corn coated in a creamy, spicy, cheesy sauce.

quiz.q: How long should corn be grilled over medium-high heat?
quiz.explanation: Grilling corn for 10-12 minutes with turning gives charred, tender kernels.

quiz.q: What is a common African twist for grilled corn?
quiz.explanation: Peri-peri butter adds a spicy, African flavour to grilled corn.

quiz.q: What is the base for a universal spicy mayo?
quiz.explanation: Mayonnaise is the creamy base for spicy mayo, mixed with ketchup and hot sauce.

quiz.q: Which ingredient thickens sweet chili sauce?
quiz.explanation: A cornstarch slurry is used to thicken sweet chili sauce.

quiz.q: What is a key ingredient in chimichurri sauce?
quiz.explanation: Chimichurri is made with fresh parsley, oil, vinegar, and garlic.

quiz.q: How long can you store homemade dipping sauces in the fridge?
quiz.explanation: Most homemade sauces should be used within 3 days for safety and freshness.

quiz.q: What is suya spice made from?
quiz.explanation: Suya spice is a Nigerian blend of ground peanuts, ginger, paprika, and cayenne.

quiz.q: For skewers, why should you leave a small gap between pieces?
options: A) To make them look better
quiz.explanation: Gaps allow heat to circulate, ensuring even cooking of all sides.

quiz.q: What is the best oil temperature for frying onion rings?
quiz.explanation: 180Â°C is ideal for crispy onion rings without being greasy.

quiz.q: What does double-frying do for Korean fried chicken?
quiz.explanation: Double-frying removes moisture and creates a very crunchy crust.

quiz.q: Which of these is a Japanese dipping sauce for tempura?
quiz.explanation: Tentsuyu is a traditional dipping sauce made with soy sauce, mirin, and dashi.

quiz.q: What is a good substitute for cotija cheese in elote?
quiz.explanation: Feta is a salty, crumbly cheese that works well as a substitute for cotija.

quiz.q: How can you keep French fries hot for sale?
options: B) Hold under a heat lamp
quiz.explanation: A heat lamp keeps fries hot and crispy without steaming them.

quiz.q: What is the main ingredient in a garlic aioli?
quiz.explanation: Garlic aioli is made by mixing minced garlic and lemon juice into mayonnaise.

quiz.q: For vegetable skewers, how long should they be grilled?
quiz.explanation: Vegetables cook faster than meat, so 5-7 minutes is enough for charring.

quiz.q: What is a common mistake when frying chicken?
quiz.explanation: Crowding lowers oil temperature, leading to greasy, unevenly cooked chicken.

quiz.q: Which sauce is best for dipping grilled meats?
quiz.explanation: Chimichurri is a savoury, herbaceous sauce that complements grilled meats.
